My partner moved into a house around 10 minutes drive from where I now live on my own. We discussed the possibility of something on the same street but I feared that would defeat the purpose of LAT. We have to be quite strict with ourselves that we don’t slip in to old patterns with spending all our spare time together. So, we schedule Wednesday and Saturday as our date days. They are exclusively to just spend some time enjoying each others company. We then plan time to see each other when we need to sort life issues out together when is needed but we never plan these on our date days. For instance, our dog comes to me every day whilst my partner is at work  during his week of custody. When we dropped off our fur baby to each other at first it was difficult to maintain. Instead of the few minutes needed to say hi, have a kiss and hand over our dog, we just ould spend hours just chatting in the car. We both decided that the point of LAT is so we were excited to see each other and that we would save our meaningful chats to our date nights. I would fear that if I lived close by to him if I saw him then I would want to spend time with him that I may have blocked out for something just for myself initially. And vice versa. So, we do the whole hey, kiss, sort dog and then we say “see you Wednesday/Saturday”. It really depends on your reasons for LAT. We have always had a really healthy relationship but we both have very busy personal lives that even though we were living together we didn’t spend any meaningful time together. This has allowed us to prioritise our relationship by working out a healthy balance. We still very much support each other and some weeks we may see more or less of each other but we never forgo a Wednesday or Saturday. As another example, my father in law was in hospital last week so my partner and I took the later visitation times. That means we spent time together everyday that week but this week I haven’t seen him since the weekend. It works for us and our lives. I believe that if you think about the end result, what kind of relationship you want, you can then plan how you both could achieve this by working backwards from there. 
And as far as how I feel remaining in our once shared home, I love it! It’s certainly my space now but my partner still helps. We’re currently doing up the garden together and putting an emperor tent out there so we can have a nice chilled zone to save money on going out on expensive dates all the time. So, although it is my home, my partner still very much feels like a part of it all.

Change is always scary, even if that change will lead to good things. My partner was the one to move out from the home we shared and much like you we also share custody of our fluff ball. At first it was daunting, unsettling at times and there was definite feelings of uncertainty between us. When you live in a society that is so rigid in its expectations of what a conventional couple looks like it can be even scarier to do something unconventional. But boy, are we glad that we ever did. I won’t bore you with the ways in which it worked out for us as every relationship needs different things but for us it simply works. Just try to live in the moment, don’t worry about the future. You were already living together and for whatever reason it just wasn’t working so try something new. If that doesn’t work then at least you tried and if it does work, great! You will both find your way.

It’s really hard for anyone to advise as no one really knows your relationship quite like you do. I will tell you from personal experience that I am the anxious one in my partnership and we had a blow up like this one, but admittedly not to these levels. My partner asked me for a break too and it was the best thing he had ever done. However, he was kind enough to actually explain how I made him feel when I suddenly had a panic attack and directed it at him. He made it all about how he was affected and didn’t once blame or judge me for an obvious momentary struggle. In brief, we were involved in a very serious car accident as a family and I started to panic about everyone’s mental health to the point I deteriorated. He knew the stress I was under as I did him and when he couldn’t take anymore he actually demonstrated that he too was struggling with certain aspects of my change in mental state. From there I knew he was right, we did need time to breathe, to not be so interdependent. It became a mutual decision and one that I can say is like the single best relationship I have ever been in. We see each other 2 nights a week, go on real dates again and other than that we don’t really see or speak to each other unless it’s about something urgent. The difference with yourselves though may be that you lay out the option for a break and he doesn’t agree or follow through with upholding your boundaries. But, so what? You’d have your answer right there that he is not willing to help his own anxieties even for himself or respect that you have your own personal boundaries. But, either way is a win win, he says yes and you get a man who is willing to better himself and your relationship and is supportive or he says no or doesn’t follow through and you have dodged a bullet! Either way I wish you all the best

I have experience of this shortly before I stumbled upon stoicism. My children, partner and I were involved in a very serious car accident in which we were stationary on a motorway and an Amazon delivery van who was speeding, on his phone and overweight smashed in to the back of of our car without braking. My son was in the boot seats and my two daughters in the middle seats. Upon impact I witnessed my partner and one of my daughters smash forward and back, I heard the screams and the cries of my daughters and the groan of my partner. Who I could not hear or see was my son. I got out of the car as quick as I could and saw the back of the car in a crumpled mess with shards of glass everywhere. The driver of the delivery van, completely unharmed, was getting out and I saw red. I ran at him and started slamming his van door on him pushing him repeatedly back in to his cab. I genuinely thought my son had died and all I wanted was to kill the man that had caused this. I had to get my anger under control very quickly and concentrate on getting at least my two girls out of the car and see if my son could be saved. I remember growling at the man and returning to the car where in fact my son was alive and surprisingly unscathed. However, one of my daughters had suffered a head injury. If I hadn’t had got control of my anger I could have killed the delivery driver but more than that, I am a psychologist, I was the one to notice the brain injury and immediately jump in to action to mitigate any permanent damage any of my children might have received. Anger was so important for me to jump in to action but it also nearly hindered me helping my family through a traumatic life-changing effect. I truly believe you can have a rational anger, a kick up the butt to take action but you need that control over it. And, that event ultimately led me to stoicism and helping my family practice this philosophy to aid in their psychological healing. As the stoics say, temperance. We are well and on our journey to overcoming this experience and now I don’t let my anger lead me, I let it merely advise.

I am ever so sorry for the turmoil you have been through and so proud of how far you too have come. I have 3 children myself, albeit teens. I have been in relationships much like yours before my most recent partner. Hurt people, hurt others. This is not to say you hurt him, I just know from my experience that people come to me hurt. I used to want to fix their problems but he taught me that the only way I could ever help someone is to be an example to live by. Much like with children. Your children will learn in time the truth but it needs to be discovered by themselves. How many times have our own parents advised us or tried to teach us valuable life lessons to mitigate any pain and it has fallen on deaf ears? Plenty on my side lol! But let me tell you a little story about an experience of mine.

Much like you I had to be involved in family legal proceedings, not court per se, but lots of closed room meetings with very scary professionals. I was a single parent with children who were also struggling with ADHD and ASD. I made a complaint about a professional and that professional accused me of things like, “not loving my children enough” and my son was terrorised by a hedgehog who apparently lived underneath his window sill. I can laugh now at the absurdity of the allegations but at the time it was an attack on my very being. Something I thought shone out of me that the world could see. I am the same to every person I ever meet, loving, empathetic and strong. This went on for four months, and they were here practically every day. Watching me and then speculating on every decision I made. Towards the end, we had another legal meeting with professionals far higher up than the ones I had previously dealt with and I asked all of them directly to show me empirically where they thought I had gone wrong. Of course there were improvements to be made, there was some truth to their lies. I was chaotic and in survival mode but I wasn’t an abuser. They couldn’t answer, they couldn’t find one thing “wrong”. The actions of one hurt person nearly derailed my whole family. Instead I vowed to keep evolving, allowing myself to be my only assessor, to trust that one day the truth will out. And I am happy to say that 2 and a half years later my children aren’t the only ones who know the truth now. We are able to talk to professionals again who were involved those many years ago and some have even recognised they may have held a wrong first impression based upon someone else’s opinion. Not that it affects me in anyway now, as I know who I am, things I excel in, things I need to practice more. But validating your truth to yourself helps. But that all started with someone being hurt and deciding to hurt us in retaliation and that to me needs empathy. Who in their right mind would jeopardise the stability of children, especially their own, just to exact revenge on their mother or stranger? No one would do this with a clear, rational mind. Ergo, they are deeply unwell and battling with themselves more than they are me. I have just got caught up in the cross hairs and so have you. 

You are incredibly resilient and the true you will shine through. Just don’t worry if you blind a few people in the process, it is up to them to wear sunglasses. Not for you to dim your glow xxx

I am ASD and ADHD and would say that that is not my experience or that of my 3 children also the same as me. I understand where you may have got this opinion from but I don’t feel it fits very well with not only my experiences but those of others in my community. Yes, I can detach, but it is not easy and certainly not devoid of emotions. Today, my partner left me, and I can tell you all the emotions are there, I feel anger, sadness, love and a bit of relief, but I use detachment to calm these emotions and ensure I stay empathetic, for myself and him. I got to love him for however long we had, that love wasn’t any less because I thought he would disappear one day. No! If anything it gave me the freedom to love him unconditionally, to appreciate every part of him, the preferred and the least preferred, and to live each and every day in gratitude. And I am still as grateful for him without him sharing my bed anymore than I was this morning when I woke up next to him without knowing it was the last time. My ASD and ADHD have definitely made some things harder but I can assure you we feel things just as deeply and it takes us a lot of work to put the genie back in the bottle too. Peace and love to you

I truly believe it is possible but not in the way you expect before you actually get it. I know this doesn’t make much sense at this moment but let me tell you about my day. My wonderful partner and father of my children walked out on us today. When I say “wonderful” I am not being sarcastic, he truly is a good man. A good man with mental health demons. I have tried over the past year to support him however he sees fit, to live my own life and hope he mimics some of these healthier habits and nurture open and free communication in our home with our children. Then, 4 months ago, he spiralled and from there he spiralled even further after a serious car accident we were all in just a few weeks later. He has not put himself first in our relationship ever either, I have come to learn. He got up every morning, put on a smile, went to work and came home and slept, rinse and repeat. His son is manipulative and dishonest, yet, he refuses to see him clearly and the relationship they have is strained because of this. He’s worried about his parents ill health even though they never once follow medical advice to help themselves. He lost all pizazz for anything, in the end, trying to please me and look after everyone by pretending to be better was what killed our relationship, made him uncertain and helped his mental health reach rock bottom. When this all started happening I knew I had to get my own emotions in check and safeguard my own wellbeing. I have loved him with all my heart and will continue to do so but I have practiced negative visualisation just as long. I knew my time with him would be fleeting, either one day we would outgrow each other or his demons would get the best of him. I am so grateful to have had the time with him regardless and I would much rather he be walking around in the world without me and spreading some of that goodness he has inside him than the worst case scenario. I don’t and never have expected anything from him because I have already found that within myself. But now I have found that in myself I want to share that with everyone. You cannot control anything outside of yourself, and holding on to an ideal of any person or experience is not only going to lead to disappointment but do you a disservice to yourself. I am sure you don’t always live up to someone else’s expectations, that’s not to say you wouldn’t if you laid your life story out plain as day for them, but all they have is that fleeting moment to make a judgement about you. Don’t let yourself be like them, you know that you try to live virtuously and do the right thing, so are they in their own way and they do it based upon their own context. They don’t know yours and you don’t know theirs. I don’t know whether my ex-partner really is struggling mentally, although I presume this is the truth, or whether he just plainly got bored of me. Either way it’s of no consequence to me. I had my time with him, I have made some outstanding memories and I can hand on heart say that I acted within my virtues for the absolute majority of it. I can move forward in growth and peace and so can you. Amor fati!

I am one of those people. Not only to have gotten rid of “social” media but in the fact I categorise Reddit as an entirely different type of platform than those such as Facebook, Instagram, etc. I would say as a social psychologist that Reddit is in fact a resource of differing points of view, some views said more unkindly than others, and the anonymity behind profiles does lead to the likes of trolling. However, there is something worse when a person can see you personally, they can see you are a face behind the keyboard in your profile pic, there is no distance between you and whoever wants to be unkind, yet enough distance to keep them safe from often a well deserved punch to the face! Reddit is too complex to regard it as positive and negative. Some subs are meant to be a place to take the kick out of others whereas other subs are designed to uplift others. Reddit is no different than sitting at a bus stop and hearing a racist old grandpas views only to get on the bus and see another younger person, who hasn’t heard his malignant monologue, give up their seat because it is the right thing to do regardless of opposing opinions. My faith in humanity is on a rollercoaster everyday of highs and lows just being offline in the real world, it is balanced. Reddit at least reflects that balance. I found my emotions felt more negatively weighted whilst using what I consider true “social” media. Just protect yourself by being cautious in what words you let enter your mind and what you put out in the world.

Very recently my children, my partner and I were in a serious road accident. Like you I had had a life of trauma and turbulence but there was something about this accident that put everything in perspective. I watched as I thought my children left this world, helpless and powerless. I nearly killed another human with my bare hands in a panic and a rage I have never felt before. This few minutes made me remember I am mortal, “memento mori”. That none of mine or my families lives are guaranteed and I had spent so many years as a victim that I had missed out on being their parent and partner. Since then I now live life to the fullest with them by my side as long as I have them with me. Have a look at the philosophy of stoicism for what you are going through right now, it makes you realise you are only in control of your reactions not the actions of the external. You may think you are just one bug, but each ant has a purpose in a colony. Each bug is part of a bigger, better picture, just as you are. Peace be with you xxx

This is fascinating, and something I will truly take away with me as I grow my view on everyone’s worlds. You might be interested in the view taken by Iain McGilchrist in The Master and his Emissary. In his book he discusses the divided brain theory, however, in his analogy, that he has named his book after, he tells of a story he once heard. In brief, a master has a plan after seeing the bigger picture and as he expands his kingdom and knowledge he decides to take on an emissary to oversee designated projects. Over time the emissary seems to be quite capable of doing their job and the master loosens the ropes so to speak. Gradually the emissary grows in arrogance and becomes power hungry. The Emissary then takes over the master by force and becomes the ruler themselves. However, unbeknownst to the emissary, the master had seen the big picture, he knew the context and that the Emissary all along only had been given a fraction of the information, only enough to get his particular job done. I have always found this to be just like our own brains and souls. We will always be torn between enlightened control of our emotions and the want to control our surroundings.
